subject: ADR-151: a rejected keystroke buffer is not an empty one
body: ADR-150 found one of these by hand and wrote the rest down as a worklist; this is the looking. AN <input type=number> HOLDS TWO THINGS: a value the page reads, and a raw keystroke buffer the page cannot see -- and when the browser cannot parse the buffer, the value it hands over is THE EMPTY STRING, the same string a box nobody touched hands over. validity.badInput is the only thing that separates them, because it is about the buffer rather than the value, and it is the one signal an ASSIGNMENT cannot produce. Which is why nothing in this kit could ask until type-text existed: every task had been driving the one half of the input space where the distinction does not exist. THE INSTRUMENT puts each box in three states and reads the page each time -- a GOOD value inside the box's own bounds ASSIGNED, BLANK ASSIGNED, and "3e" TYPED with badInput confirmed true afterwards. GOOD != BLANK IS THE CONTROL, and it is what makes the second comparison a finding: without it every box read only when a button is pressed joins the worklist and the worklist means nothing. BLANK == BAD is the finding. WHAT COUNTS AS TELLING THEM APART IS WHAT THE READER WOULD SEE -- a sentence, a mark (aria-invalid, a class), or a sentence in an element carrying no id at all -- so elements are keyed by id where they have one and by where they sit in the document where they do not, one key per element, and a clock takes only its own key out of the comparison instead of every card around it. Ids that move on their own are found by reading the page twice at rest and dropped. THE PAGE GETS EVERY CHANCE TO SAY SOMETHING: a verdict only moves UP a ladder -- unreachable, inert, cannot-tell, tells -- and a box is re-asked in every state the page can be put in until it tells, because the finding is 'in no state did the page say a different thing' and not 'it said nothing in the state I happened to look at'. IT FOUND 63 BLIND BOXES ON 16 PAGES, of 185 measured on 22. The sharpest row is experiment-guide.html with twelve -- the page ADR-150 had just taken WHOLE at 52 of 52 fields. Taking a page whole means every field was ENTERED; it never meant every field was asked this question, and until there was an instrument nobody could have known the difference. ALL 63 ARE FIXED, AND MOSTLY NOT IN THE PAGES. The Field Entry Kit goes 1.3.0 to 1.4.0: its stepper and its instrument field check badInput before they read .value, mark the row, and print the box's own name with what happened to it -- and blur no longer repaints the old value over the reader's characters, which used to erase the evidence and take the message down with it, the page quietly deciding it knew better. One change, re-emitted into nineteen consumers: 39 of the 63, across ten pages. A second FEK change covers the plain number boxes those pages build themselves -- seven more on three pages -- by ONE DELEGATED LISTENER in capture phase rather than a wrapper per box, because the boxes a page builds later (a row added, a grid opened) have to be covered too and a guard that only knew about the boxes present at load would go quiet exactly when the sheet gets long. THE REST IS PAGE CODE: the guide's four factors emitted NOTHING when rejected, and emitting nothing is how that page says 'the neutral value', so a typed factor silently became 1 (or 0 for distance); its grader fell back to seed 42 and 3 passes; its six measurement cells said 'waiting for every cell', which is what they say about a cell nobody filled in, and now name which cell and why. ecology-lab's exporter had checked badInput since ADR-148 and the two live workbenches beside it had not, answering a rejected buffer with 'enter non-negative counts'. tree-visualizer's select k-th answered with the same em dash an empty box gets -- and the fix found its twin in rank-of, which shares a line and shared the bug. BOTH ENDS OF THE RATCHET WERE MEASURED WITH THE SAME INSTRUMENT. The first reading said 33, taken while the report channel was still keyed by id alone -- it could not see the pages that answer in unnamed elements, which is most of what the Field Entry Kit mounts. Rather than publish a fall from one instrument's number to another's, the pages at the ADR-150 commit were checked out and measured again with the final instrument: 63. A ratchet whose two ends were measured differently is not a ratchet. THE CEILING IS ZERO on all 22 pages that carry number boxes, so the next box added that reads a rejected buffer as blank fails the day it is added, with no flag, because run_all runs an audit with no arguments. A box that genuinely should not care is declared with a REASON in the ledger; nothing is declared today. verify_badinput 32, mutate_badinput 24 with 1 known equivalent. HELD: the audit says a page renders a DIFFERENT thing, not a RIGHT thing, and grading the wording is nobody's instrument yet; 107 of the 185 boxes are INERT -- read only when a button is pressed -- and this audit does not press buttons, so whether the reports they feed are blind is unmeasured and stated rather than hidden, which is the obvious next slice; three boxes on releve.html could not be focused in any state the audit could reach and are reported UNREACHABLE rather than as passing; type=text boxes holding numbers have no badInput at all, so there is nothing there to be blind to, and whether a page should have used type=number is a design question this does not touch; and the audit costs about eight minutes over the kit, three page states per box and one keystroke at a time, which is the price of asking a question no assignment can ask.
